levels.name: Lvl 1
levels.title: Vector Spaces
levels.description: Axioms, fields, vectors, and linear combinations.

tasks.title: Read: Chapter 1 (Vector Spaces) in 'Linear Algebra Done Right' by S. Axler
Watch: 'Vectors, what even are they?' by 3Blue1Brown on YouTube
Theory: Write the formal definitions of a vector space over a field F and linear independence
Practice: Prove that the set of functions {f: R -> R} form a vector space over R

quiz.question: The Rank-Nullity Theorem states that:
quiz.explanation: For a linear transformation T: V -> W on a finite-dimensional vector space V, dim(V) = dim(range T) + dim(null T).

levels.name: Lvl 2
levels.title: Subspaces & Span
levels.description: Direct sums, spans of subsets, and subspace verification criteria.

tasks.title: Verify that intersection of two subspaces U and W is always a subspace.
Work through 5 problems on linear span in Axler §1.C.

quiz.question: Which of the following is NOT required for U to be a subspace of V?
options: U is closed under vector addition
U is closed under scalar multiplication
quiz.explanation: Subspaces only require 0 in U, closure under addition, and closure under scalar multiplication.

levels.name: Lvl 3
levels.title: Linear Independence
levels.description: Linear combinations, testing independence, and coefficients.

tasks.title: Read: Linear Independence and Linear Dependence Lemma in §2.A.
Construct a proof for the linear dependence lemma.

levels.name: Lvl 4
levels.title: Bases and Dimension
levels.description: Spanning lists, minimal spanning sets, and dimension invariance.

tasks.title: Study: Every spanning list can be reduced to a basis.
Solve dimension equations for sum of subspaces: dim(U + W).

levels.name: GATEWAY QUIZ
levels.title: Vector Spaces Gateway Quiz
levels.description: Complete the gateway assessment to unlock Unit II: Linear Transformations.

gatewayQuiz.title: Gateway Quiz
gatewayQuiz.description: ATTEMPTS ALLOWED • Minimum 40% required to unlock Unit II

questions.question: If V and W are vector spaces over F, then dim(V x W) is:
questions.explanation: The dimension of the direct product V x W equals dim(V) + dim(W).

questions.question: Which of the following polynomials are linearly independent in P_2(R)?
questions.explanation: The standard monomial basis {1, x, x^2} is linearly independent.

questions.question: The zero vector in a vector space V is:
questions.explanation: By the axioms of vector spaces, the additive identity is strictly unique.

questions.question: If a list of vectors v1, ..., vn spans V, then:
options: Any linearly independent list in V has length <= n
Any linearly independent list in V has length >= n
questions.explanation: Fundamental theorem: Length of linearly independent list <= length of spanning list.

questions.question: The intersection of any collection of subspaces of V is:
options: Never a subspace unless both are trivial
Only a subspace if V is real
questions.explanation: Arbitrary intersections of subspaces are always subspaces.
